subject: Request: transient data access exemption for production triage (FinHealth)
messages:
From: Alan Park <alan.park@finhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: FinHealth Security <security@finhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: transient access needed for payments failures investigation

Hi Vivek,

We are seeing a spike in failed payment events overnight that appear to be correlated with model responses used by our reconciliation flow. Our engineering team needs a short window to pull recent inference traces and request payloads so we can reproduce the error.

We understand Redwood's standard retention and deletion policies, but this is a production outage affecting customer payments. Can you advise the quickest path to get a timeboxed exception for access to the last 72 hours of logs/kv cache for our tenant? We can accept a limited scope and audit trail.

I attached a small snippet from our monitoring and an internal incident ticket. Please let me know what information you need from our side to expedite.

Thanks,
Alan
Alan Park
Director, Platform Engineering
FinHealth

Attachments: finhealth-incident-log-snippet.txt
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: transient access needed for payments failures investigation

Team — forwarding Alan's ask. TL;DR: FinHealth requests a short-lived exemption to retrieve the last ~72h of inference traces and request payloads for a payments outage. They explicitly accept limited scope and auditing.

What I need:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether we can support a 72-hour extraction scoped to tenant X without violating existing deletion policies? If we need Legal signoff, flag next steps.
- Dev: what is the minimal artifacts we should hand over to keep the window as small as possible (e.g., request IDs, partial traces, truncated prompt text vs full payload)? Also include instrumentation steps to ensure we don't leak PII.

I want to propose: 24-hour snapshot first (fast), escalate to 72-hour only if repro fails. Will that satisfy them?

Please reply with actionable checklist and an estimate (hours) to provision this. We need to get back to FinHealth within the hour.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: legal-approvals@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: transient access needed for payments failures investigation

Vivek — quick guidance from ops/legal triage after a brief sync with Dev:

1) Scope: a 24-hour, timeboxed extract limited to inference metadata, request IDs, and token-level deltas (no full customer PII fields). If repro can't be achieved, we can expand to 72 hours but only after a formal approval form and an explicit justification from FinHealth.

2) Controls:
- Access is read-only and performed by a named Red team member (Dev).
- Data will be staged to a secured, ephemeral S3 bucket with server-side encryption and access logs enabled.
- We will produce a signed audit record (who accessed what, why, and when) and push that to the security mailbox.

3) Approvals: Legal wants the signed exception form attached (prod-exception-request-form.pdf). Please have FinHealth sign and return ASAP. If they cannot sign, we need a customer POC email explicitly authorizing the access and the limited fields.

4) Timeline: Dev estimates ~3 hours to gather the 24-hour snapshot and place it in the secure staging area once we have either the signed form or an explicit POC email. Expanding to 72 hours adds ~2 more hours and requires a manager-level sign-off from Security.

Dev — please confirm the artifact list you will extract and any sanitization steps.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Alan Park <alan.park@finhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: FinHealth Security <security@finhealth.com>, ops@finhealth.com
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: transient data access exemption for production triage (FinHealth)

Thanks Vivek/Marissa —

We can sign the exception form immediately. Attaching a signed copy in my reply (sending via our external signing system), and we authorize the 24-hour snapshot as first step. If your team cannot reproduce from 24 hours, we authorize escalation to 72 hours with the same controls and audit record.

Also confirming the POC for FinHealth will be me (alan.park@finhealth.com) and Rajesh Malhotra (r.malhotra@finhealth.com). Please proceed and confirm when the staging link is available.

—Alan

FinHealth
